Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.9 · Exercise 45

Volume Inside a Bumpy Sphere

Problem

The surfaces ρ=1+51​sinmθsinnϕ have been used as models for tumors. The "bumpy sphere" with m=6 and n=5 is shown. Use a computer algebra system to find the volume it encloses.

Reading the shape

The surface is written in spherical coordinates. The symbol ρ is the distance from the origin, θ is the angle around the z-axis, and ϕ is the angle from the positive z-axis. With m=6 and n=5 the surface is

ρ=1+51​sin6θsin5ϕ.

The factor 51​sin6θsin5ϕ is the bump. It never exceeds 51​ in absolute value, so the radius stays between 0.8 and 1.2 and the solid is star-shaped about the origin. The six bumps around the equator come from sin6θ, and the five rings of bumps from the pole to the equator come from sin5ϕ.

A meridian shows the bump in one plane. Along the meridian θ=π/12 the factor sin6θ equals 1, so that meridian reaches ρ=1.2. Along θ=π/4 it equals −1, so that meridian shrinks to ρ=0.8.

Setting up the integral

In spherical coordinates the volume element is dV=ρ2sinϕdρdϕdθ. The solid is the set of points with 0≤ρ≤1+51​sin6θsin5ϕ, 0≤ϕ≤π, and 0≤θ≤2π. The radial integral is immediate:

V=∫02π​∫0π​∫0ρ(θ,ϕ)​ρ2sinϕdρdϕdθ=31​∫02π​∫0π​(1+51​sin6θsin5ϕ)3sinϕdϕdθ.

Expanding the cube

Write u=51​sin6θsin5ϕ. Then

(1+u)3=1+3u+3u2+u3.

Each term is integrated against sinϕ over the sphere of directions. Three of the four terms vanish, and each one vanishes for a reason.

The linear term. It contains sin6θ, and

∫02π​sin6θdθ=0,∫0π​sin5ϕsinϕdϕ=0.

The second integral vanishes because sin5ϕ is odd about ϕ=π/2 while sinϕ is even there.

The cubic term. It contains sin36θ, and

∫02π​sin36θdθ=0,∫0π​sin35ϕsinϕdϕ=0.

The square term. This term survives. The square removes the sign, because sin2 has period π while sin has period 2π:

∫02π​sin26θdθ=π,∫0π​sin25ϕsinϕdϕ=99100​.

The second value follows from sin25ϕ=21​(1−cos10ϕ):

∫0π​sin25ϕsinϕdϕ=21​∫0π​sinϕdϕ−21​∫0π​cos10ϕsinϕdϕ=1−21​⋅992​=99100​,

where cos10ϕsinϕ=21​(sin11ϕ−sin9ϕ) and ∫0π​sinkϕdϕ=k2​ for odd k.

Adding the surviving terms

The constant term.

∫02π​∫0π​sinϕdϕdθ=2π⋅2=4π.

The square term.

3(51​)2π⋅99100​=253π​⋅99100​=334π​.

Add the two results and divide by 3:

V=31​(4π+334π​)=31​⋅33136π​=99136π​≈4.3157.

Checking the value

The unit sphere holds 4π/3≈4.1888. The bumpy sphere must be slightly larger, because the mean of ρ over all directions is 1 while the mean of ρ3 is larger than 1. The computed ratio confirms this:

4π/3V​=3334​≈1.0303,4π3V​=3334​≈1.0303.

Three independent computations give the same value 4.315723. They are the term-by-term integrals above, a double quadrature of the exact integral, and a Monte Carlo average of ρ3 over uniformly distributed directions. The Monte Carlo value is 4.315040, which agrees to four digits.

Answer

The surface encloses the volume

V=31​∫02π​∫0π​(1+51​sin6θsin5ϕ)3sinϕdϕdθ=99136π​≈4.3157.

Only the constant term and the square term of the expanded cube contribute. The linear term and the cubic term give zero.

Notation

SymbolMeaning
ρThe distance from the origin in spherical coordinates, ρ≥0. On this surface ρ is a function of the two angles.
θThe angle around the z-axis, measured from the positive x-axis, 0≤θ≤2π.
ϕThe polar angle, measured from the positive z-axis, 0≤ϕ≤π.
dV=ρ2sinϕdρdϕdθThe volume element in spherical coordinates. The factor ρ2sinϕ is the Jacobian.
m=6, n=5The numbers of bumps around the equator and from pole to pole. The product sinmθsinnϕ makes the pattern repeat.
star-shapedA solid is star-shaped about the origin when every ray from the origin meets its boundary once. Here that holds because ρ(θ,ϕ)>0 for every pair of angles.
mean over directionsThe average of a quantity over all directions, with weight sinϕdϕdθ and total 4π.

Verification

  • part1_step1.py expands (1+u)3, tests every term, and prints the vanishing integrals ∫02π​sin6θdθ, ∫0π​sin5ϕsinϕdϕ, ∫02π​sin36θdθ, and ∫0π​sin35ϕsinϕdϕ. It then prints ∫02π​sin26θdθ=π, ∫0π​sin25ϕsinϕdϕ=100/99, the square term 4π/33, and V=136π/99. A final direct integration confirms the result.
  • part1_step2.py confirms 4.315723 by double quadrature and 4.315040 by a Monte Carlo average over four million directions.
  • part1_figure1.py draws the surface. part1_figure2.py draws the meridians at θ=π/12 and θ=π/4 against the unit sphere.
